attributes.name: Endurance
attributes.about: How long they can keep going. The biggest part of marathon readiness.

attributes.name: Pace
attributes.about: How fast they can hold a steady effort. Turns readiness into a faster finish.

attributes.name: Strength
attributes.about: Leg and core strength. Resists injury and keeps form late in the race.

attributes.name: Recovery
attributes.about: How quickly fatigue clears between sessions.

attributes.name: Pacing Knowledge
attributes.about: Knowing what effort to hold. Makes race day less of a gamble.

exercises.name: Easy run
exercises.why: Conversational-pace running builds the aerobic base that every marathon is made of, with little fatigue. Most of a good plan is easy running.
exercises.cue: Hold a pace they could chat at.

exercises.name: Long run
exercises.why: The weekly long run teaches the body to keep going for hours. It is the single most marathon-specific session, and the hardest one to keep someone going through.
exercises.cue: Keep them going when the distance starts to bite.

exercises.name: Tempo run
exercises.why: A sustained 'comfortably hard' effort raises the pace a runner can hold. Essential for a time goal, less useful when the goal is simply to finish.

exercises.name: Intervals
exercises.why: Short fast efforts with recoveries build speed. They are the most tiring session in the plan and the easiest to overdo.
exercises.cue: Decide each repeat: continue, ease off, or stop.

exercises.name: Goblet squat
exercises.why: Strong legs and hips absorb thousands of footstrikes. Strength work lowers injury risk and holds form late in the race.

exercises.name: Walking lunges
exercises.why: Single-leg strength mirrors running, where every stride lands on one leg. It builds balance as well as strength.

faults.fault: Front knee drifting past the toes
Torso leaning over the front leg

exercises.name: Step-ups
exercises.why: A gentle, joint-friendly way to build leg strength. A good first strength exercise for someone new to training.

exercises.name: Skipping
exercises.why: Quick, springy contacts train the feet and calves and improve running rhythm. High impact, so keep it short for new runners.

exercises.name: Core circuit on the mats
exercises.why: Planks and bridges keep the trunk stable so the legs work efficiently when tired. Low fatigue; fits into any session.

exercises.name: Mobility and foam rolling
exercises.why: Easy mobility work helps tired legs feel fresher and trains the habit of recovering properly. It removes fatigue instead of adding it.

exercises.name: Rowing machine
exercises.why: Low-impact aerobic work. Builds endurance without the pounding of running, ideal for someone whose joints are still adapting.
exercises.cue: Long, smooth strokes at a steady effort.

exercises.name: Barbell back squat
exercises.why: Heavier loading builds strength faster than dumbbells once the movement is learned.
